title: Fire & Smoke Mitigation Cleaning Authorization, Deposit and Cancellation Terms
content:
These terms govern the cleaning authorization of a Fire & Smoke Mitigation job, the self-pay deposit that must be in place before cleaning starts, the customer's right to cancel a dispatch before signing, and the point at which cleaning is complete.

## Terms

> The job must be in dispatched status when the cleaning authorization is signed or the dispatch is cancelled. The cleaning authorization is signed by the owner or the owner's authorized agent. Cleaning may start on a self-pay job only after customer payments posted to the job total at least the tier's self-pay deposit. A customer may cancel the dispatch before signing; the service call stays billable, and board-up already installed stays billable on tiers where it does. Cleaning is complete when the supervisor's final walk finds no residual soot or odor and the equipment is removed.

## 1. Signing the cleaning authorization

1.1 The cleaning authorization is signed while the job is in dispatched status, and it is signed by the owner or the owner's authorized agent.

1.2 Signing moves the job from dispatched to authorized, and the date signed is recorded on the job.

## 2. Cancelling before signing

2.1 While the job is in dispatched status, the customer may decline cleaning and cancel the dispatch before signing. The cancellation moves the job from dispatched to cancelled and records the date cancelled.

2.2 Once the job has left dispatched status, neither signing nor cancellation under these terms is available.

2.3 On cancellation, the service call stays billable. Board-up already installed stays billable on the tiers where the company's securing price list marks board-up as billable on cancellation; on the other tiers it does not stay billable.

| Item on a dispatch cancelled before signing | Billable after the cancellation? |
|---|---|
| Service call | yes, on every tier |
| Board-up already installed, on a tier where it stays billable on cancellation | yes |
| Board-up already installed, on a tier where it does not | no |

## 3. Deposit before cleaning starts

3.1 On a self-pay job, cleaning may start only after the customer payments posted to the job total at least the tier's self-pay deposit. Reaching the deposit exactly is enough.

3.2 The start of cleaning and deodorization moves the job from authorized to cleaning and records the start date.

Hypothetical deposit check, for a hypothetical self-pay deposit of 800.00:

| Customer payments posted to the job | Total against the deposit | Cleaning may start? |
|---|---|---|
| one payment of 500.00 | 500.00, short of 800.00 | no |
| 500.00 and 300.00 | 800.00, exactly the deposit | yes |
| 500.00 and 450.00 | 950.00, above the deposit | yes |

The deposit condition is stated for self-pay jobs.

## 4. Cleaning complete

Cleaning is complete when the supervisor's final walk finds no residual soot or odor and the equipment has been removed. The completion test has two parts, both of which hold at completion: the final walk finds no residual soot or odor, and the equipment is removed. Completion moves the job from cleaning to cleaning complete and records the completion date.

## Status path under these terms

dispatched, then authorized on signing, then cleaning when cleaning and deodorization begin, then cleaning complete on the final walk; or dispatched, then cancelled when the customer declines cleaning before signing.
